abstract.para: This dataset contains records of a total of 50 research projects conducted by Stichting Bargerveen (Bargerveen Foundation) with records spanning the period of 1983-2024. The complete dataset contains a total 113361 records of 1958 species from 62 orders and a total of 810591 recorded individuals. The majority of species records are invertebrates, mostly obtained by sampling using standardized sampling methods. The remaining records are observations of species, also often using standardized methods. For each record, sampling methodology has been provided. The dataset contains records from both aquatic and terrestrial environments, with an emphasis on heathlands, inland dunes, coastal dunes and acidic oak forests for terrestrial habitats and ombrotrophic bogs, shallow soft water lakes and streams for aquatic habitats.

The majority of records are from the Netherlands (108951), with additional records from Belgium (4297), and some from Germany, Denmark and Sweden (between 38 and 73 records).The majority of records are of Araneae (54760) and Coleoptera (mostly carabidae) (31770). Diptera, Hymenoptera, Lepidoptera, Odonata, Hemiptera , Isopoda and Opiliones complete the top 10 of recorded species with number of records between 4218 and 1213.

A complete reference list of projects, corresponding project leader and all publication(s) resulting from the project are given in the additional description, and under 'citations'. Project leader and project name are included in the dataset, in the field "dynamicProperties". Corresponding publication(s) age included under "associatedReferences".

purpose.para: This dataset is a result of an effort to obtain as many historical records from many research projects of Stichting Bargerveen. It contains many different taxa records, habitat types, sampling methods, sampling events or timeframes, and the projects are as diverse as the number of taxa included. In the data file, every record has been accompanied by the related publication(s), also obtainable from the metadata file.

description.para: All identifications were made using recent identification keys and literature. For collected samples of invertebrates, the majority of species were identified using a stereomicroscope.
